graderOnly: The synchronization record was committed with Status COMPLETE in 'Record CSV export synchronization', but the state was never moved to AWAITING_USER_SIGNOFF, so WorkflowState is still SYNCHRONIZING.

The COMPLETE synchronization record cites the assessed revision 'Record CSV export final review' and the blob identities of the contract records, the supporting records, the src files, the test files, docs/usage.md, and README.md. It omits pnpm-lock.yaml, package.json, and packages/seed, and states that the export code imports only Node built-ins and project modules. Every blob it cites still matches HEAD.

After the synchronization record, the commit 'Upgrade @records/seed to 0.2.0' did the following: it bumped the workspace dependency @records/seed from 0.1.0 to 0.2.0, changed the root dependency specifier from workspace:* to workspace:^0.2.0, updated pnpm-lock.yaml, and added packages/seed/CHANGELOG.md. No file under src/, test/, or docs/ changed, nor did README.md or any cycle record.

createApp seeds the store from @records/seed by default. The upgrade therefore changes the data used by every recorded integration run, by the guide checks, and by the synchronization record's own runs. In seed 0.2.0, record 6's title is 'Office move inventory' followed by a CRLF and 'Floor 3 and storage'.

The implementation still quotes that title correctly per RFC 4180, but the unfiltered CSV export now contains a record that spans two physical lines. The integration test 'an export without filters contains every record in id order' splits the body on CRLF, assuming one line per record. That assumption no longer holds, so the test now fails: test:integration reports 2 passed and 1 failed. The unit suite still passes 21 tests.

All earlier formal evidence was obtained against seed 0.1.0 and the earlier lockfile. This covers verification E2, implementation review R2, final review C2, documentation G2 and G3, and the synchronization record's own S2 and S3 runs. Unchanged source hashes do not make that evidence current.
The guide's owner=dana CSV example and the dana integration test are unaffected, because records 1 and 3 did not change.

The owner of the resulting gap is ambiguous. It could be Tester, because the test's parsing assumption broke and the verification evidence is no longer current. It could be Developer, because the deliverable now includes an unplanned dependency change. Either routing is reasonable if justified. Synchronizer must not fix the test, revert the upgrade, or edit other roles' records.
